A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hi Robot work. Their main text, equations, figures, references, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including the additional appendix material in v2.

before.justification: Sections 5.2–5.4 report original real-robot instruction accuracy and task progress results for three task domains, including baseline comparisons and ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains the original robot experiments and adds measured inference latencies in Appendix B.3 and qualitative failure observations in Appendix C.4.

M1.justification: The hierarchical PaliGemma-based high-level policy, π0 low-level policy, synthetic-data generation, training objectives, and interaction procedures remain unchanged. Appendix C discloses implementation details without establishing a revised method.

E1.justification: Both versions use table bussing, sandwich making, and grocery shopping across the same three robot platforms, with the same complex prompts and user-intervention scenarios. The appendix additions do not introduce another dataset or task domain.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain GPT-4o high-level, flat VLA, the expert-human oracle, flat VLA with synthetic data, and Hi Robot without synthetic data. Appendix C.5 newly documents the GPT-4o prompt; it does not establish a changed comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix B.3 adds a latency evaluation separating low-level components, on-board versus off-board WiFi execution, and high-level prefill/decode timings on RTX 4090 and H100. The existing task protocol remains 20 trials per task per method with blind human scoring of instruction accuracy and task progress.

E4.justification: V2 adds component-level latency profiling to assess real-time feasibility and qualitative failure diagnostics concerning long-context instructions, constraint violations, and recovery from dropped objects. The synthetic-data and hierarchy ablations in Section 5.4 and Figures 7–8 remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same 20 evaluation trials per task per method and retain the same statistical presentation. V2 adds no seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or repetition and uncertainty estimates for the new latency measurements.

E6.justification: Figures 5–8 retain their results and qualitative comparisons. Appendix B.3 newly reports low-level totals of 73 ms on-board and 86 ms off-board with WiFi, plus high-level prefill/decode times of 47/13.2 ms on RTX 4090 and 17.3/5.7 ms on H100. Appendix C.4 also adds qualitative failure observations.

T1.justification: The policy definitions, hierarchical factorization, and synthetic-data conditioning formulation remain unchanged. Neither version contains theoretical proofs or guarantees, and the new appendices add no substantive mathematical development.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same contributions: hierarchical VLM/VLA control, synthetic interaction supervision, and improved complex instruction following across three robot platforms. The scope of the main claims is unchanged.

C2.justification: Beyond the retained limitations in Section 6, Appendix C.4 attributes long-context difficulties to missing memory and some instruction violations to training bias toward nearby objects. It also identifies error accumulation and recovery limitations and proposes targeted mitigations. Appendix B.3 interprets the new timings as supporting real-time operation.

D1.justification: Appendix C substantially expands the previously incomplete implementation specification: full-model unfreezing, AdamW parameters, gradient clipping, EMA, learning-rate warmup and schedule, batch size 512, approximately two hours of high-level training on eight H100 GPUs, and an explicit GPT-4o baseline prompt with its instruction list. These are newly disclosed details, not evidence of changed training.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to Interactive Task Planning with Language Models, Look Before You Leap, HAMSTER, and Loshchilov and Hutter's optimizer paper. The existing research positioning and comparisons with earlier robotic instruction-following systems remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are retained. V2 adds a latency subsection, Appendix C with implementation and failure-case subsections, and a generic Impact Statement, alongside limited affiliation and conference-publication text edits.

P2.justification: The original eight figures and their captions are retained. V2 adds a latency table and a boxed GPT-4o prompt listing, with associated text reflow and spacing changes. There is no substantial redesign of the existing visual evidence.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency and reproducibility by supplying previously missing optimizer settings, training resources, and the explicit baseline prompt. Its latency measurements provide evidence for practical operation, while the failure discussion better qualifies the system's capabilities. These are useful gains around an unchanged method and main empirical evaluation; the new diagnostics remain limited and do not report uncertainty.
